title: How Much Can Urban Nature Help?
text:
Researchers wanted to estimate how much nature-based solutions could help cities reduce greenhouse-gas emissions. Their computer model counted direct effects, such as trees and green roofs storing carbon, and indirect effects, such as shade reducing energy use or making walking more attractive than driving.

The model also compared different strategies across different urban settings instead of assuming that one solution would work equally well everywhere. Researchers applied the model to 54 European cities. Across those cities, nature-based solutions were estimated to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions by about 17% on average, with larger reductions in some places.

Nature-based solutions were not enough to bring cities to net zero on their own. The researchers described them as one part of a broader approach that can also include cleaner electricity and better public transport. The amount they could contribute differed by strategy and by city.
